summary: Reviewed blind source inventories and fidelity contracts against shared-omission, unused-fact and source-evidence failure modes. Formal representation is rendered independently of candidate prose promises; semantic labels remain explicit model judgments.
findings: Two source-only requests precede candidate exposure; exact commitment union cannot vote away a minority claim.
Every claim/candidate pair requires a check. Missing evidence is NOT_ESTABLISHED, not contradiction.
Unused facts are excluded from executable-meaning text, preventing a declared but unapplied exception from looking implemented.
Deterministic cues catch a particular shared inventory omission; they do not prove arbitrary English completeness.
Unit tests inject semantic judgments to verify contracts; real source-first model behavior is reserved for A7.
Bidirectional prompt checks original claim support and unsupported extra candidate restrictions, with uncertainty preserved.
